MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Reliability over a mission, availability over time, maintainability under given resources and total restoration delay answer different questions and cannot be substituted by one mean. Guard: Under regenerative cycles with finite positive mean up and down times, long-run time availability is E[U]/(E[U]+E[D]); exponential hazards are sufficient in a two-state Markov model but not necessary for the regenerative ratio.
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.MISSION_OR_SERVICE: A declared mission interval and restoration/support conditions for the item or service. Current scope: Finite-mission survival, point availability, interval availability and full delay distributions as separately named quantities.
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND: Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.OPERATING_PROFILE: Declared demands, workload mix, duty cycle, mode changes and maintenance states.
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Separate reliability, availability, maintainability, supportability and durability claims
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.REQUIRED_FUNCTION: A declared mission interval and restoration/support conditions for the item or service. Current scope: Finite-mission survival, point availability, interval availability and full delay distributions as separately named quantities.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.REASON: No distinct recovery claim is made by this candidate.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.REASON: The property does not itself claim redundancy benefit; any redundant implementation must invoke ERM-P008/ERM-P009.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS: Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Use observed event counts, interval-union downtime and a short delay decomposition when a stochastic model is unnecessary.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CLAIM: Reliability over a mission, availability over time, maintainability under given resources and total restoration delay answer different questions and cannot be substituted by one mean. Guard: Under regenerative cycles with finite positive mean up and down times, long-run time availability is E[U]/(E[U]+E[D]); exponential hazards are sufficient in a two-state Markov model but not necessary for the regenerative ratio.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY: Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Frequent short outages and one long outage yield99% time availability but differ in mission continuity; overlapping diagnosis and spare delivery must not be added twice.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.COVERAGE: Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Choose prevention, repair, spares or accepted interruption according to the specified consequence.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS: Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Reliability over a mission, availability over time, maintainability under given resources and total restoration delay answer different questions and cannot be substituted by one mean. Guard: Under regenerative cycles with finite positive mean up and down times, long-run time availability is E[U]/(E[U]+E[D]); exponential hazards are sufficient in a two-state Markov model but not necessary for the regenerative ratio.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MODEL: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Separate reliability, availability, maintainability, supportability and durability claims
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN: Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

R005.profile_scope: The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

current_claim.audit_question: What required or dormant function can fail silently, how long could it remain failed, and which tested demand does the check represent?
current_claim.bearer: A required path, standby function or protective function that can fail unnoticed.
current_claim.change_note: Retains the native insight without universal elimination or testing quotas.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Trace the actual path once and exercise the protective function directly; accept a low-consequence single point explicitly.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Spare proof test, inspection interval, redesign or accepted outage.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Testing itself consumes spare life and maintenance attention; retire a proof test when the protected demand or mechanism is removed.
current_claim.counterexample: A spare exists but its credential expired; a component survives while its only power or recovery path is unavailable.
current_claim.criterion: Identify the demand, dormant state, observable test and consequence of leaving it latent; avoid pretending the test covers other fault classes.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Formal structural reasoning and scoped historical/incident examples; no generic inspection interval is estimated.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Relative to the stated mission and fault model, identify minimal failure sets and latent duration. Single-failure tolerance does not imply tolerance of common causes or all multiple failures.
current_claim.mechanism: Exercises or checks a dormant function before a real demand, or removes the unique dependency.
current_claim.model_domain: Minimal sets are structural properties of a specified model; latent failure probability and inspection benefit require an observation/repair process.
current_claim.negative_scope: No requirement to eliminate every single point regardless of consequence, feasibility and cost.
current_claim.positive_scope: Dormant backups, protective channels and required service paths.
current_claim.proposition: A single required dependency or latent protective failure can defeat a claimed mission or fault tolerance; relevant exposure can be eliminated, detected, repaired or explicitly accepted.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Test sensitivity, induced harm, demand rate, repair capability and relevant common causes.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.current_scope_judgment: Relative to the stated mission and fault model, identify minimal failure sets and latent duration. Single-failure tolerance does not imply tolerance of common causes or all multiple failures. No requirement to eliminate every single point regardless of consequence, feasibility and cost.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: A spare exists but its credential expired; a component survives while its only power or recovery path is unavailable. Formal structural reasoning and scoped historical/incident examples; no generic inspection interval is estimated.

DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Author cases are constructed arithmetic/logical witnesses only. No deployed demonstration or physical/operational test was performed.

FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Minimal sets are structural properties of a specified model; latent failure probability and inspection benefit require an observation/repair process. Formal structural reasoning and scoped historical/incident examples; no generic inspection interval is estimated.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Historical attribution retained, with current typed genealogy and exact fresh scopes. No original executed-prompt or earliest-priority inference.

INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed operator incident accounts support reported mechanisms at those events, not prevalence or independently verified countermeasure effects.

LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Selected reported operating/experimental evidence, if listed; no new empirical dataset received or reanalyzed. Empty list means no such fresh direct evidence assigned to this claim.

OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed normative/practitioner/owner sources explain selected mechanisms, intent or currentness at their access scopes; they are not independent causal efficacy studies.

REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No independent replication of the author cases or target field effect. Related source versions, chapters and reports are grouped in the source dependence register.

TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No target-system transfer established. Test sensitivity, induced harm, demand rate, repair capability and relevant common causes.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.AMBIGUITY_GROUPS: Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION: Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.DETECTION_COVERAGE: Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.FALSE_ALARM_COST: Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.ISOLATION_RESOLUTION: Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.LATENCY: Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: A single required dependency or latent protective failure can defeat a claimed mission or fault tolerance; relevant exposure can be eliminated, detected, repaired or explicitly accepted. Guard: Relative to the stated mission and fault model, identify minimal failure sets and latent duration. Single-failure tolerance does not imply tolerance of common causes or all multiple failures.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.MISSED_DETECTION_COST: Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.OBSERVABLES: Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION: Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.RECOVERY_COVERAGE: Count a detected event as successfully restored or contained only for the separately declared action outcome and denominator. A true detected event remains detected even when restoration is absent or unresolved. Detection, isolation, containment and restoration coverage are reported separately.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES: One fault, or one fault plus an undetected latent condition, defeats required function. Current limitation: No requirement to eliminate every single point regardless of consequence, feasibility and cost.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING: Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY: A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.CONTROL: Exercises or checks a dormant function before a real demand, or removes the unique dependency.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCIES: Test sensitivity, induced harm, demand rate, repair capability and relevant common causes.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.DETECTION: Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.END_EFFECT: One fault, or one fault plus an undetected latent condition, defeats required function. Current limitation: No requirement to eliminate every single point regardless of consequence, feasibility and cost.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE: One fault, or one fault plus an undetected latent condition, defeats required function. Current limitation: No requirement to eliminate every single point regardless of consequence, feasibility and cost.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.LATENT_CONDITION: Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.LOCAL_EFFECT: Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT: Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.PROPAGATION_PATH: Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Single-point and latent-failure exposure control
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.RESIDUAL_RISK: Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.REASON: The candidate is a supporting mechanism or rejected proxy rather than a standalone mission claim.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.REASON: No distinct recovery claim is made by this candidate.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.CLAIMED_TOLERANCE: The specified number/class of faults tolerated while meeting required function or an accepted degraded state.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.COMMON_CAUSE_COUPLINGS: Specification, design, implementation, environment, supplier, maintenance, configuration and operational coupling.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.DEGRADED_MODE: Declared reduced capability and exit conditions.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.FAILURE_DOMAINS: Physical, power, network, control-plane, state, software, supplier, operator and maintenance domains.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_EVIDENCE: Address actual shared causes and the joint event law. Statistical independence is required only by formulas or claims that use it; dependent paths may still provide a positive rescue increment. Copy count or labels alone do not establish separation.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: A single required dependency or latent protective failure can defeat a claimed mission or fault tolerance; relevant exposure can be eliminated, detected, repaired or explicitly accepted. Guard: Relative to the stated mission and fault model, identify minimal failure sets and latent duration. Single-failure tolerance does not imply tolerance of common causes or all multiple failures.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.REDUNDANCY_FORM: Active, standby, voting, diverse, replicated or alternate-path redundancy as explicitly declared.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.STANDBY_LATENCY_OR_DORMANCY: Dormant faults, activation delay and cold/warm/hot readiness are measured when applicable.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.STATE_CONSISTENCY: The takeover state and authority must be current, complete and semantically valid.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.SWITCHOVER_COVERAGE: Detection, decision, transfer, state synchronisation and post-transfer functional success.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Evidence appropriate to the stated protection claim, including a direct deterministic result or a model at its exact premises where adequate. A general architecture or field-rate claim needs correspondingly broader evidence; no universal live-test or field-study bundle is imposed.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.REASON: The property is primarily a design/operation mechanism; its validation still follows ERM-P026–P029.

current_claim.audit_question: Which failure mechanisms are shared, what joint evidence exists, and is a conservative assumption being mistaken for an observed fact?
current_claim.bearer: Joint failure behavior of channels or dependencies under specified causes and exposure.
current_claim.change_note: Qualifies the native cheap-path instruction to treat copies as one domain: a permissible bound is not a factual identity.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Use conservative bounds or one-domain treatment as a declared decision assumption where justified; preserve less pessimistic possibilities as unresolved.

R008.profile_scope: The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

current_claim.audit_question: Exactly which otherwise-failing cases does the added channel rescue, what does it add that can fail, and which numerical formula really follows from the dependence evidence?
current_claim.bearer: A concrete redundant architecture, including controllers, transfer, state and capacity.
current_claim.change_note: The native name says only with credible independence and the mature form uses a multiplication-like list, but its mechanism and profile already require common-cause analysis. Strict statistical independence as a necessary condition is refuted by C02; practical failure-domain separation is a different, qualitative interpretation. The current wording removes that ambiguity without imputing a numerical product formula or wholesale rejection to the native record.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: One simpler system, a manual spare or explicit downtime can dominate an added controller; no blanket preference is established.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Admit a bounded fault-tolerance claim or choose single-component repair/manual spare/accepted downtime.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Compare acquisition, energy, shared updates, testing, diagnosis, state synchronization and eventual retirement, not replica count alone.
current_claim.counterexample: C02 shows positive benefit under high positive correlation, no gain under perfect shared cause, and net loss after an unreliable serial controller.
current_claim.criterion: Name the tolerated fault set, rescue cases, joint-dependence assumptions, transfer/state/capacity conditions and added failure/cost paths.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Conditional probability derivation and constructed cases are strong within model; historical experiment and scoped architecture sources restrict but do not quantify any deployed design.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: For ideal OR success events A and B, P(A union B)-P(A)=P(B intersect not A). This is positive exactly when the added channel rescues a positive-probability set. Real architecture must include switchover, voter, state, load and common causes.
current_claim.mechanism: Alternative capacity/path supplies the required function on selected failures; transition or common-control failures can erase the increment.
current_claim.model_domain: The identity is exact for the stated event model. The event correspondence and joint probabilities need system evidence.
current_claim.negative_scope: No general claim that replication, N-version development, multicloud or additional replicas are sufficient or always harmful.
current_claim.positive_scope: Independent and dependent redundancy with explicit benefit and added-risk analysis; active/standby/voting require their own model.
current_claim.proposition: Redundancy can improve a named function when the added path succeeds in some otherwise failing cases and its added failure mechanisms do not outweigh that benefit. Statistical independence is needed for the usual product shortcut, not for every positive redundancy benefit.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Actual failure distribution, capacity margin, detection/switchover coverage, failure of recovery mechanisms, configuration and economic or separate safety constraints.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.FAILURE_DOMAINS: Physical, power, network, control-plane, state, software, supplier, operator and maintenance domains.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.INDEPENDENCE_EVIDENCE: Address actual shared causes and the joint event law. Statistical independence is required only by formulas or claims that use it; dependent paths may still provide a positive rescue increment. Copy count or labels alone do not establish separation.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Redundancy can improve a named function when the added path succeeds in some otherwise failing cases and its added failure mechanisms do not outweigh that benefit. Statistical independence is needed for the usual product shortcut, not for every positive redundancy benefit. Guard: For ideal OR success events A and B, P(A union B)-P(A)=P(B intersect not A). This is positive exactly when the added channel rescues a positive-probability set. Real architecture must include switchover, voter, state, load and common causes.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Dependence-aware redundancy with explicit rescue, transition and added-risk conditions
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.REDUNDANCY_FORM: Active, standby, voting, diverse, replicated or alternate-path redundancy as explicitly declared.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.STANDBY_LATENCY_OR_DORMANCY: Dormant faults, activation delay and cold/warm/hot readiness are measured when applicable.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.STATE_CONSISTENCY: The takeover state and authority must be current, complete and semantically valid.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.SWITCHOVER_COVERAGE: Detection, decision, transfer, state synchronisation and post-transfer functional success.
REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Evidence appropriate to the stated protection claim, including a direct deterministic result or a model at its exact premises where adequate. A general architecture or field-rate claim needs correspondingly broader evidence; no universal live-test or field-study bundle is imposed.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.REASON: The property is primarily a design/operation mechanism; its validation still follows ERM-P026–P029.

native_audit_unique.POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY: Availability gain versus switchover/state-synchronisation complexity.
native_audit_unique.QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT:
- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate redundancy only with credible independence, coverage and switchover?
- Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?
- Are the supposed redundant channels actually separate failure domains, and is detection, switchover, state transfer and degraded capacity covered?
- Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?

current_claim.audit_question: Which propagation path is actually interrupted, what useful function survives, and can the containment action itself cause a worse loss?
current_claim.bearer: A boundary or action that limits a specified fault's propagation.
current_claim.change_note: Preserves native containment breadth while explicitly permitting material partial protection without full causal closure.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: A simple resource cap, manual feature restriction or no-op can be preferable to a new cell architecture.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Partition, rate-limit, disable a feature, stop a component or accept a bounded exposure.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Isolation can reduce capacity and visibility or create state divergence; remove stale barriers only after revisiting the protected path.
current_claim.counterexample: Two apparent service cells share a control plane; disabling one data-plane route leaves the actual common failure path intact.
current_claim.criterion: List the propagation path removed, receiving function preserved, possible false isolation and residual shared mechanisms.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Primary architectural mechanisms, an operator incident and an explicit truth-table construction; not measured general risk reduction.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Given a fault set and an implemented barrier/action, establish which effects are blocked and which paths remain. A drawn boundary alone does not implement isolation.
current_claim.mechanism: Separates communication, load, control or state to stop selected propagation while accepting restricted function.
current_claim.model_domain: A graph cut or logical guard is internal evidence; real resources, state, control and authority must instantiate it.
current_claim.negative_scope: No implication that isolation is always safe, that all dependencies are cut, or that containment is equivalent to repair.
current_claim.positive_scope: Partial containment under unresolved cause and bounded manual as well as automatic actions.
current_claim.proposition: Containment is a bounded restriction on downstream effects; it may protect remaining functions without diagnosing or restoring the failed part.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Barrier implementation, safe ambiguity action, available capacity and residual external premises.

current_claim.audit_question: Detected out of which fault population, by when, with which missed classes and false alarms, and what additional premise is needed for a beneficial action?
current_claim.bearer: A detector, its target fault/failure set and an observation opportunity.
current_claim.change_note: The native detection claim survives; the shared recovery field will be explicitly scoped as recovery rather than detection coverage.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: A direct manual functional check can be more informative than proxy health instrumentation for an infrequent reversible decision.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Triage, containment, manual checking or a decision to gather more evidence.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Instrumentation consumes performance, maintenance and attention. Retire signals that have no useful discrimination or receiving decision.
current_claim.counterexample: C03 detects60of100fault opportunities but restores15; reporting only15as detection erases information, while calling60restored overclaims.
current_claim.criterion: Declare target set, detected count/weight, missed population, false-alarm denominator and latency; separately examine the action's effect.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Primary taxonomy/review and exact conditional arithmetic; no detector or field dataset was evaluated.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Count detections against the declared fault population, not only recovered faults. Weighting by mode or exposure must be explicit; an incomplete fault list does not become universal coverage.
current_claim.mechanism: Signals a fault or failed function early enough to support a possible intervention or investigation.
current_claim.model_domain: Sensitivity, false-alarm probability and latency are different conditional quantities. Their measured values need a valid labelled population.
current_claim.negative_scope: No requirement that every detection identifies a unique cause or proves restoration; no generic requirement for expensive independent infrastructure.
current_claim.positive_scope: Direct functional tests, manual checks and partial instrumented coverage.
current_claim.proposition: Detection coverage is the fraction or conditional probability of a specified target population detected within a stated condition and latency; detection can provide useful information before isolation, containment or restoration succeeds.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Ground truth, missed classes, label error, latency, distribution shift and an available beneficial action.

current_claim.audit_question: Which uncertainty actually changes the remedy, and can a bounded useful action proceed while other causes remain unresolved?
current_claim.bearer: A diagnosis or ambiguity set used for a particular intervention.
current_claim.change_note: Static suspicion does not establish a wholesale defect: native mature/cheap-path fields already reject forced root-cause certainty. Clarify shared RECOVERY_COVERAGE only; preserve this no-change finding.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Use the shared remedy when the guard is supported; defer expensive isolation if it cannot alter the decision.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Select a replaceable unit, a safe reversible response, manual investigation or an admitted unknown.
current_claim.cost_retirement: More precise diagnosis may consume the recovery window. Preserve logs needed for later discrimination without imposing unlimited retention.
current_claim.counterexample: A restart restores a transient state without identifying whether the trigger was a software timing fault or hardware disturbance; the local recovery does not prove either explanation.
current_claim.criterion: State the ambiguity group, what evidence rules hypotheses in/out, what the action needs to know and the consequences if a remaining hypothesis is true.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Randell's primary design explicitly separates recovery and later diagnosis; no claim that all symptoms admit a common safe remedy.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: For an action under uncertainty, examine its consequence over the remaining plausible causes. Exact root-cause closure is not a universal prerequisite for detection, containment or bounded restoration.
current_claim.mechanism: Avoids a forced single-cause narrative and directs only decision-relevant discrimination.
current_claim.model_domain: An ambiguity set and conditional action rule can be formally specified; the truth of hypotheses and safety of the remedy remain empirical/domain claims.
current_claim.negative_scope: No presumption that every unresolved cause makes action invalid; no presumption that acting on symptoms proves the cause.
current_claim.positive_scope: Action-sufficient diagnosis, symptom-directed repair and deferred investigation.
current_claim.proposition: Diagnosis should resolve enough uncertainty to support the intended action; several causes can remain plausible when they share an adequately supported remedy.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Plausible-set adequacy, action authority, reversibility where relevant, costs, and residual risk.

current_claim.audit_question: Which specific loss can this path recover from, what evidence exists, and which change would invalidate it?
current_claim.bearer: A backup/rebuild/reconstitution path with state, tools, permissions and a receiving function.
current_claim.change_note: Preserves the native anti-backup-theater claim while replacing unconditional periodicity with meaningful freshness and applicable obligations.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Recreate reproducible stateless artifacts and perform one functional check; use existing current evidence when new testing adds no discrimination.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Keep/modify a backup plan, replace it with rebuild, accept loss or schedule a proportionate exercise.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Account for storage, credentials, exercise disruption, staff and obsolete formats; retire redundant paths only after protecting remaining obligations.
current_claim.counterexample: Readable backup bytes cannot restore service when the only decryption credential was lost with the original system.
current_claim.criterion: Trace what is recoverable, under which loss, how long and with which residual data loss; identify evidence invalidators.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Scoped current NIST guidance and technical/incident mechanisms; no independent efficacy trial or actual restoration conducted.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Exercise or other adequate evidence should cover the actual claim; refresh is triggered by material changes, stale assumptions or a binding obligation, not by an arbitrary universal frequency.
current_claim.mechanism: Challenges accessibility, integrity, compatibility, missing authority and integration before relying on recovery.
current_claim.model_domain: A restoration demonstration establishes the tested path and configuration. It does not establish success under every loss scenario.
current_claim.negative_scope: No production disruption or recurring full rehearsal quota follows from this research.
current_claim.positive_scope: Isolated tests, existing valid demonstrations and cheap deterministic rebuild checks where sufficient.
current_claim.proposition: Possessing a backup does not establish restore capability. A claimed path needs evidence that the required state and function can be reconstituted under the relevant configuration and resource assumptions.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Backup trust, state currency, resource availability, protected authority, dependencies and realistic load.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

native_audit_unique.QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT:
- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate backup, restore and reconstitution paths must be exercised and validated?
- Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?
- Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?
- What population, denominator, model, confidence, censoring rule and expiry condition bound the reliability claim?

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION: Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.DETECTION_COVERAGE: Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.FALSE_ALARM_COST: Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.ISOLATION_RESOLUTION: Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.LATENCY: Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Condition-based or predictive maintenance earns a benefit claim through an observable precursor, timely feasible intervention and net consequence compared with an adequate alternative; predictive score alone is insufficient. Guard: The precursor and uncertainty must correspond to the deployed population, failure mechanism and decision horizon. Weak evidence can justify an exploratory bounded trial, not a universal superiority claim.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.MISSED_DETECTION_COST: Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.OBSERVABLES: Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION: Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.RECOVERY_COVERAGE: Count a detected event as successfully restored or contained only for the separately declared action outcome and denominator. A true detected event remains detected even when restoration is absent or unresolved. Detection, isolation, containment and restoration coverage are reported separately.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES: No stable precursor; sensor drift; domain shift; uncertain RUL ignored; maintenance action ineffective; false alarms dominate; lead time shorter than logistics delay. Current limitation: No automatic transfer of RUL models across machines, duty cycles, sensors or intervention regimes; no universal preference for digital twins/AI.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING: Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY: A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.CONTROL: Uses earlier information to schedule a beneficial action while avoiding premature or missed maintenance.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCIES: Representative labels/censoring, precursor stability, available interventions, causal counterfactual, uncertainty and resource cost.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.DETECTION: Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.END_EFFECT: No stable precursor; sensor drift; domain shift; uncertain RUL ignored; maintenance action ineffective; false alarms dominate; lead time shorter than logistics delay. Current limitation: No automatic transfer of RUL models across machines, duty cycles, sensors or intervention regimes; no universal preference for digital twins/AI.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.INITIATING_FAULT_OR_FAILURE: No stable precursor; sensor drift; domain shift; uncertain RUL ignored; maintenance action ineffective; false alarms dominate; lead time shorter than logistics delay. Current limitation: No automatic transfer of RUL models across machines, duty cycles, sensors or intervention regimes; no universal preference for digital twins/AI.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.LATENT_CONDITION: Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.LOCAL_EFFECT: Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT: Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.PROPAGATION_PATH: Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.RESIDUAL_RISK: Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.REASON: The candidate is a supporting mechanism or rejected proxy rather than a standalone mission claim.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.REASON: No distinct recovery claim is made by this candidate.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.REASON: The property does not itself claim redundancy benefit; any redundant implementation must invoke ERM-P008/ERM-P009.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS: Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Fixed replacement, inspection or run-to-failure may be sufficient or superior; retained uncertainty is legitimate.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CLAIM: Condition-based or predictive maintenance earns a benefit claim through an observable precursor, timely feasible intervention and net consequence compared with an adequate alternative; predictive score alone is insufficient. Guard: The precursor and uncertainty must correspond to the deployed population, failure mechanism and decision horizon. Weak evidence can justify an exploratory bounded trial, not a universal superiority claim.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY: Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: A more sensitive predictor triggers many costly unnecessary replacements for a rare failure and performs worse than a cheap inspection policy.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.COVERAGE: Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Inspect, repair, schedule replacement, gather labels or retain a simpler baseline.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS: Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Condition-based or predictive maintenance earns a benefit claim through an observable precursor, timely feasible intervention and net consequence compared with an adequate alternative; predictive score alone is insufficient. Guard: The precursor and uncertainty must correspond to the deployed population, failure mechanism and decision horizon. Weak evidence can justify an exploratory bounded trial, not a universal superiority claim.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MODEL: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN: Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

native_audit_unique.POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY: Sensitivity/early warning versus false maintenance and model drift.
native_audit_unique.QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT:
- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value?
- Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?
- Which enumerated failures can the diagnostic detect and isolate within the required latency, and what are the false-positive and false-negative costs?
- What population, denominator, model, confidence, censoring rule and expiry condition bound the reliability claim?

R023.profile_scope: The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

current_claim.audit_question: Which engineering decision did the failure evidence inform, and what supports the claim that the disposition actually affected the relevant mechanism?
current_claim.bearer: A test/field failure-reporting and correction process.
current_claim.change_note: Retains closed feedback and rejects administrative closure as its own evidence.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Repair an obvious reversible defect and directly verify the function; record a justified no-change disposition.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Fix, investigate, narrow a claim, retain a control, accept a residual or retire unnecessary process.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Feedback consumes engineering attention and can reward bookkeeping; consolidate or retire loops with no meaningful consumer while preserving necessary reporting.
current_claim.counterexample: Failure counts decline only because usage falls; closing every ticket does not identify the residual risk.
current_claim.criterion: Can the reader identify the observed failure, exposure, decision, intervention if any, result and unresolved premises without inferring causality from administrative status?
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Owner scope/status for2155/189 and scoped primary growth/standard discussion; their unread full bodies are not normative implementation authority.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Record a material failure's disposition and supporting evidence at the warranted scale; unresolved causality or accepted risk can be an explicit outcome rather than manufactured closure.
current_claim.mechanism: Carries observed failures into candidate cause assessment, targeted change or no action, verification and comparable subsequent observation.
current_claim.model_domain: Reporting/traceability supports inquiry; a closed loop label does not prove an intervention caused reliability growth.
current_claim.negative_scope: No board, ticket-volume, universal root-cause or action-change quota.
current_claim.positive_scope: A one-defect local correction as well as a sustained FRACAS programme.
current_claim.proposition: A feedback loop is useful when observations can alter or confirm a specific design, maintenance or acceptance decision and the disposition preserves what is known about exposure and correction.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Reporting incentives/completeness, recurrence definition, configuration comparability, intervention quality and observational limits.

current_claim.audit_question: What changed in the failure mechanism, where was it deployed, and what observation would distinguish effectiveness from reduced exposure or luck?
current_claim.bearer: A particular corrective change and the recurrence mechanism or function it targets.
current_claim.change_note: Preserves native bounded causality and explicitly allows partial risk reduction without global root-cause closure.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: A direct regression/functional check plus deployment evidence can settle a narrow deterministic claim.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Accept a local fix, continue observation, narrow the effect claim or seek a different cause.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Surveillance and extra controls have costs; retire them when evidence and consequence justify, not when the ticket counter demands it.
current_claim.counterexample: A defect patch passes its targeted reproducer but a different configuration still fails; a lower incident count under less usage says little about the patch.
current_claim.criterion: Identify before/after mechanism behavior, deployment identity, regression scope and recurrence opportunity, then state precisely what remains unproven.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Primary report mechanisms and supplier accounts; planned supplier mitigations are not independently verified successful corrections.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: A deterministic local defect can be corrected and checked without proving every rare failure cause. Wider recurrence reduction needs comparable opportunities, uncertainty and competing explanations.
current_claim.mechanism: Removes or blocks a specific failure route, or reduces its probability, while possibly introducing regressions.
current_claim.model_domain: A reproducer can show a local pre/post behavioral change; population causal effects require additional design/data assumptions.
current_claim.negative_scope: No requirement for indefinite surveillance until zero residual risk; no inference from ticket status or curve fit.
current_claim.positive_scope: Bounded effective correction with remaining uncertainty and justified no-change when evidence confirms an existing control.
current_claim.proposition: Correction effectiveness is stronger when the change addresses a supported mechanism, is actually deployed and passes an appropriate discriminator; a falling field trend alone cannot establish causality.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Reproducer validity, deployment reach, other causes, comparable profile and confounding.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.LOCAL_EFFECT: Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT: Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.PROPAGATION_PATH: Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Accept a local fix, continue observation, narrow the effect claim or seek a different cause.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS: Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Correction effectiveness is stronger when the change addresses a supported mechanism, is actually deployed and passes an appropriate discriminator; a falling field trend alone cannot establish causality. Guard: A deterministic local defect can be corrected and checked without proving every rare failure cause. RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MODEL: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Corrective-action effectiveness and recurrence control
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN: Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. current_claim.audit_question: Which mode-specific relationship justifies the conversion to use conditions, and is this an assessment, a screen or an exploratory stress test?
current_claim.bearer: A mapping from accelerated stress evidence to a use-condition lifetime or failure process.
current_claim.change_note: Native equivalence condition is necessary in many models but not sufficient; the current claim names the mapping and mixed-mode burden.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Field-like stress, engineering margin or targeted destructive tests can answer a bounded design question without an accelerated lifetime claim.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Estimate life, set a qualification margin, explore weaknesses or decline quantitative extrapolation.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Acceleration saves time but requires characterization and can create false precision; retire obsolete extrapolations after material changes.
current_claim.counterexample: C07has unchanged competing hazards with factors10and2; dividing their combined accelerated rate by10understates use hazard.
current_claim.criterion: Identify what the test was designed to learn, mode-specific mapping, censored observations, uncertainty and unsupported stress regions.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Full NIST technical page, scoped primary report and current standards metadata; no accelerated experiment performed and paid62506clauses not read.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Specify each relevant mechanism, its stress response, competing modes and the range of supported extrapolation. If mechanisms change, restrict the claim or model that change explicitly.
current_claim.mechanism: Obtains informative failures sooner while attempting to preserve a modelled relation to use conditions.
current_claim.model_domain: Conditional acceleration equations can be valid; their parameters and mechanism correspondence require physical/experimental evidence.
current_claim.negative_scope: No direct lifetime proof from HALT limits, no common acceleration factor automatically shared by different modes.
current_claim.positive_scope: Mechanism-supported ALT and separately labelled HALT, screening and destructive exploration.
current_claim.proposition: Quantitative accelerated-to-use inference needs a justified stress-life/failure-process mapping and mode composition; merely exposing an item to harsher conditions or retaining nominally the same mechanism is insufficient.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Physical failure mechanism, stress uniformity, sample dependence, parameter uncertainty and external transfer.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.

current_claim.criterion: Trace missingness, censoring, report selection, changed thresholds and profile strata before interpreting change.

current_claim.audit_question: Which software/use/environment process is being measured, and which assumptions justify the fitted model or its transfer beyond the observed version?
current_claim.bearer: Software behavior under a specified version, state/input profile and environment.

current_claim.cost_retirement: Model fitting and profile upkeep need decision value; retire unsupported forecasts rather than continuously refitting them into apparent certainty.
current_claim.counterexample: The same defect rate can yield very different user failure rates under different inputs; C13matches a power-law mean without being an NHPP.
current_claim.criterion: State the failure event, profile/version, activation mechanism, process assumptions and limits of extrapolation.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Primary scoped technical literature and own model counterexample; Musa/Goel–Okumoto/Jelinski–Moranda original bodies remain inherited citations, not newly read proofs.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Condition on relevant state, inputs, concurrency, randomness and infrastructure. A deterministic program argument requires those conditions; modern systems need not repeat behavior from a superficially identical request.
current_claim.mechanism: Tests and observations sample activations; fixes change behavior and can introduce new faults or alter usage.
current_claim.model_domain: Profile-weighted failure probability and formal correctness are different claims. Growth-model fitting requires process assumptions beyond a plotted mean.
current_claim.negative_scope: No direct transfer of hardware aging distributions to code, no universal software MTBF and no guarantee from low defect density.
current_claim.positive_scope: Functional/property tests, profile-based statistics and formal results with explicit assumptions.
current_claim.proposition: Software reliability concerns failure activation under use, not physical wear of unchanged code; faults, operational profiles and corrective changes can interact so that a generic failure-rate curve is not a universal law.

MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.PROPERTY: SLI/SLO and error-budget governance as a scoped decision aid
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.REQUIRED_FUNCTION: A user/mission-relevant outcome remains within an agreed loss budget over a declared denominator/window, with action when exhausted. Current scope: An explicit service policy with known exclusions and supplementary tail/cohort evidence.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.REASON: No distinct recovery claim is made by this candidate.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.REASON: The property does not itself claim redundancy benefit; any redundant implementation must invoke ERM-P008/ERM-P009.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS: Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Direct incident/change judgment may be clearer for low-volume or nonservice tasks.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CLAIM: An SLI/SLO and error-budget rule can organize a legitimate service trade-off when measurement, tolerance and decision authority are defined; the ratio itself does not authorize release freezes or other actions. Guard: Bind the indicator to a function, denominator/window and accepted objective; state policy exceptions and authority. Aspirational/non-action objectives and small-service direct judgment are valid alternatives.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY: Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: The aggregate SLO passes while a cohort fails; an error-budget overrun caused by an excluded event can imply different action under different declared policies.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.COVERAGE: Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Continue, pause or target changes, revise the objective or use a more suitable measure.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS: Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: An SLI/SLO and error-budget rule can organize a legitimate service trade-off when measurement, tolerance and decision authority are defined; the ratio itself does not authorize release freezes or other actions. Guard: Bind the indicator to a function, denominator/window and accepted objective; state policy exceptions and authority. Aspirational/non-action objectives and small-service direct judgment are valid alternatives.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MODEL: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: SLI/SLO and error-budget governance as a scoped decision aid
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN: Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.

current_claim.audit_question: Exactly what does this green result prove, what can still be wrong, and can the probe or its response contribute to the outage?
current_claim.bearer: A health probe and the specific function/symptom it observes.
current_claim.change_note: Preserves the native distinction while treating a layered stack as an optional design, not the universal mature property.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: One direct user-visible operation can dominate many internal status bits when it covers the relevant function.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Investigate, contain, repair or retain a simpler check.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Deep probes consume load, can mutate state and require credentials; remove duplicates that add no meaningful coverage.
current_claim.counterexample: A false health-check transition causes unnecessary failover and capacity loss; a sorted-and-same-sum check accepts a nonpermutation.
current_claim.criterion: Compare the observed predicate with the required function and inspect where both could fail together or the probe could cause harm.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Operator account, primary design text and an explicit logical counterexample; not a validation of any deployed probe.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: State what the probe exercises, its own dependencies, observation latency, false results and side effects. An independent path is useful only insofar as it addresses a shared observation failure.
current_claim.mechanism: Detects end-to-end symptoms and separates them from internal clues used for diagnosis.
current_claim.model_domain: Probe pass is an observation conditional on its oracle and coverage; the full semantic requirement may be stronger.
current_claim.negative_scope: No mandatory monitoring stack or unconditional failover on a failed health signal.
current_claim.positive_scope: Direct local/manual tests and layered monitoring when each layer adds discrimination.
current_claim.proposition: A functional probe can supply stronger evidence about a named outcome than an internal liveness bit, but neither establishes diagnosis or all service semantics.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Oracle adequacy, representative transaction, access, probe health, sampling and feasible response.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.current_scope_judgment: State what the probe exercises, its own dependencies, observation latency, false results and side effects. An independent path is useful only insofar as it addresses a shared observation failure. No mandatory monitoring stack or unconditional failover on a failed health signal.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: A false health-check transition causes unnecessary failover and capacity loss; a sorted-and-same-sum check accepts a nonpermutation. Operator account, primary design text and an explicit logical counterexample; not a validation of any deployed probe.

DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Author cases are constructed arithmetic/logical witnesses only. No deployed demonstration or physical/operational test was performed.

FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Probe pass is an observation conditional on its oracle and coverage; the full semantic requirement may be stronger. Operator account, primary design text and an explicit logical counterexample; not a validation of any deployed probe.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Historical attribution retained, with current typed genealogy and exact fresh scopes. No original executed-prompt or earliest-priority inference.

INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed operator incident accounts support reported mechanisms at those events, not prevalence or independently verified countermeasure effects.

LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Selected reported operating/experimental evidence, if listed; no new empirical dataset received or reanalyzed. Empty list means no such fresh direct evidence assigned to this claim.

OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed normative/practitioner/owner sources explain selected mechanisms, intent or currentness at their access scopes; they are not independent causal efficacy studies.

REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No independent replication of the author cases or target field effect. Related source versions, chapters and reports are grouped in the source dependence register.

TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No target-system transfer established. Oracle adequacy, representative transaction, access, probe health, sampling and feasible response.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.AMBIGUITY_GROUPS: Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION: Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.DETECTION_COVERAGE: Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.FALSE_ALARM_COST: Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.ISOLATION_RESOLUTION: Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.LATENCY: Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: A functional probe can supply stronger evidence about a named outcome than an internal liveness bit, but neither establishes diagnosis or all service semantics. Guard: State what the probe exercises, its own dependencies, observation latency, false results and side effects. An independent path is useful only insofar as it addresses a shared observation failure.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.MISSED_DETECTION_COST: Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.OBSERVABLES: Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION: Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: End-to-end health checks and symptom-versus-cause separation
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.RECOVERY_COVERAGE: Count a detected event as successfully restored or contained only for the separately declared action outcome and denominator. A true detected event remains detected even when restoration is absent or unresolved. Detection, isolation, containment and restoration coverage are reported separately.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES: Shallow probe; cached/static response; monitor bypasses dependency/state/authentication; probe shares failure; symptom automatically labelled root cause. Current limitation: No mandatory monitoring stack or unconditional failover on a failed health signal.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING: Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.CONTROL: Detects end-to-end symptoms and separates them from internal clues used for diagnosis.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.END_EFFECT: Shallow probe; cached/static response; monitor bypasses dependency/state/authentication; probe shares failure; symptom automatically labelled root cause. Current limitation: No mandatory monitoring stack or unconditional failover on a failed health signal.

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.LOCAL_EFFECT: Loss, corruption, delay, false indication or degraded performance at the initiating item.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT: Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.PROPAGATION_PATH: Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.PROPERTY: End-to-end health checks and symptom-versus-cause separation
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.RESIDUAL_RISK: Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

current_claim.audit_question: What shared normal or recovery dependency could defeat the claimed protection, and what evidence supports the fallback when it is absent?
current_claim.bearer: A required function and its normal/recovery dependency paths.
current_claim.change_note: Retains mapping as decision support rather than mandatory inventory ceremony.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Trace one important consumer path and one restoration path before building a universal map.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Simplify, isolate, cache, add a compatible fallback or accept the residual.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Maps stale and extra providers add coordination/configuration; retire unused edges/controls only after checking remaining consumers.
current_claim.counterexample: Data-plane copies survive but depend on the same DNS/control-plane planner; internal state returns while external authorization remains unavailable.
current_claim.criterion: Name each dependency's required role, shared mechanisms, fallback validity and recovery sequencing/capacity.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: One detailed operator report, model exposition and historical definitions; not an independent census of cloud dependencies.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Trace the relevant mission and loss scenario; static edges do not encode timing, capacity, authority or the full joint failure distribution.
current_claim.mechanism: Reveals hidden single points, shared control/identity and restoration dependence that limit claimed isolation.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.COVERAGE: Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Correct, narrow, confirm or retire a claim/control, or decide that existing evidence already suffices.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS: Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.

Guard: Choose a worthwhile unresolved question, adequate observation and supported containment/return conditions. Justified continuation is a valid outcome. Live production injection is outside this commission.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MODEL: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN: Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. current_claim.audit_question: Can recovery attempts exceed surviving capacity, and which restriction or cheaper response best preserves the authorized function?
current_claim.bearer: A resource-limited service and its admission/retry/recovery policy.
current_claim.change_note: Retains native overload awareness and separates a mathematical stability check from operational optimization.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Reject early or remove an amplifying action when that protects the named function; adding another layer is not automatically necessary.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Backoff, shed load, limit concurrency, disable a harmful retry/failover loop, increase capacity or accept delay.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Reserve capacity costs energy/resources; avoid permanent controls that merely conceal a removed bottleneck.
current_claim.counterexample: C10's90requests/s are below100capacity but20%one-retry amplification raises attempts to108; the AWS account describes related recovery/backlog interactions at one event.
current_claim.criterion: Include normal, retry and recovery work in the load model; check who bears rejection/delay and when the system can drain.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Operator account and constructed inequality; no queueing performance benchmark or universal overload threshold.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: A simple constant-rate fluid model needs arrival work below service capacity for stability; real queues add variability, deadlines, finite buffers and changing capacities.
current_claim.mechanism: Limits amplification, reserves useful capacity or sacrifices selected work to permit recovery.
current_claim.model_domain: The load inequality is conditional mathematics, not a production retry budget or proof of all tail latency.
current_claim.negative_scope: No automatic inference that more spare capacity is always economical or that rejecting load is harmless.
current_claim.positive_scope: Measured or conservatively bounded capacity policies with explicit consequence.
current_claim.proposition: Recovery work competes for capacity; retries, failover and backlog replay can turn a partial failure into overload unless their resource effects and consumer priorities are considered.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Service work distribution, current capacity, retry semantics, fallback capacity, deadlines and accepted losses.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE: Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS: Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS: Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS: Protect priority function and recover without unstable positive feedback or exhaustion of the remaining fault-tolerant capacity. Current scope: Measured or conservatively bounded capacity policies with explicit consequence.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.INITIATING_FAILURE: Retry storm; thundering herd; failover target underprovisioned; cache cold start; load shedding removes critical work; no admission control. Current limitation: No automatic inference that more spare capacity is always economical or that rejecting load is harmless.
